title: Localization comparisons for the ringed projection mate
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $R_Y$ be a sheaf of commutative rings and fix an identification $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and derived tensor computed by K-flat total complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For an object $V\to Y$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $U=X\times_YV$ and let $f_V$ be the induced morphism from the localized topos of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ at $U$ to that of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ at $V$. Write $j_V^*$ and $j_U^*$ for restriction to these localized sites and restrict the coefficient sheaves there. For $E\in D(R_X)$ and $P,M,N\in D(R_Y)$ there are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$j_V^*Rf_*E\cong R(f_V)_*j_U^*E,\qquad j_U^*Lf^*P\cong Lf_V^*j_V^*P,\qquad j_V^*(M\otimes^L N)\cong j_V^*M\otimes^L j_V^*N.$$
Under these isomorphisms, restriction of the adjoint-of-counit projection map for $(f,E,P)$ is exactly the adjoint-of-counit projection map for $(f_V,j_U^*E,j_V^*P)$, including the canonical shift comparisons. A morphism in $D(R_Y)$ is an isomorphism if, for every site object $V$, some covering $\{V_i\to V\}$ makes all its restrictions to $V_i$ isomorphisms. No quasi-compactness or uniform cohomological bound is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] to the base-change functor $u_f$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Its object $u_f(V)$ is exactly $U=X\times_YV$, an object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, not an assumed open subscheme. We obtain the ringed localization square, the ordinary pullback comparison $f_V^*j_V^*\cong j_U^*f^*$, and the ordinary direct-image comparison $\beta^0:j_V^*f_*\cong(f_V)_*j_U^*$. For $W\to V$ the latter identifies both module sections with $G(X\times_YW)$; the $R_Y(W)$-actions agree because the localized ring map is the restriction of the specified map $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. That same pullback square restricts this ring isomorphism to $(f_V)^{-1}(R_Y|_V)\cong R_X|_U$.

source.place: Tags 03CF and 04J0, localization of the site morphism

proof.text: Restriction on module sheaves is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Thus $H^q(j_T^*A)=j_T^*H^q(A)$, directly by its preservation of kernels and cokernels, and termwise restriction induces the derived restriction functors. The pullbacks $f^*$ and $f_V^*$ are also exact: their coefficient maps are isomorphisms (Step 1), so their underlying abelian functors are inverse image, exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]; kernels and cokernels of module sheaves are computed on underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Consequently the ordinary square of Step 1, applied termwise to any representative of $P$, induces $j_U^*Lf^*P\cong Lf_V^*j_V^*P$. Here $Lf^*$ is exactly the termwise exact functor specified in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; the same construction applies on the localized sites. Naturality for derived morphisms follows by inversion of quasi-isomorphisms from naturality of the ordinary square.

source.place: Restriction discussion immediately before 08FI; 04J0 with isomorphic coefficient maps

proof.text: Choose a K-injective resolution $E\to I$ in module sheaves using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Exact restriction sends it to a quasi-isomorphism $j_U^*E\to j_U^*I$, and [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] makes $j_U^*I$ K-injective. The definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] represents $Rf_*E$ by $f_*I$, and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] represents $R(f_V)_*j_U^*E$ by $(f_V)_*j_U^*I$. Restricting the former complex gives exactly the latter by $\beta^0$ of Step 1 in every degree. This is the desired $\beta:j_V^*Rf_*E\cong R(f_V)_*j_U^*E$. Maps between K-injective representatives give the same comparison: [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents all derived morphisms into them by homotopy classes, and additive restriction and pushforward preserve these homotopies. Thus the comparison is natural and independent of the resolution.

source.place: 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; proof method of 0FN5, lemma-localize-cartesian-square-modules (the site morphism is the one from Step 1)

proof.text: The restriction morphism of ringed topoi has module pullback $j_V^*$, since its ring map identifies the restricted ring with $R_Y|_V$. It is exact by Step 2, so $Lj_V^*=j_V^*$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to this morphism to obtain the canonical natural comparison $j_V^*(M\otimes^LN)\cong j_V^*M\otimes^Lj_V^*N$. More explicitly, choose flat K-flat representatives of $M,N$; the cited theorem preserves their K-flatness under pullback and its tensor comparison is induced on their direct-sum total tensor complexes. Restriction preserves the bidegrees and the tensor differential $d_M\otimes1+(-1)^a1\otimes d_N$. The same construction applies to $j_U^*$.

The comparison $\beta$ from Step 3 is the exchange mate of the pullback square from Step 2. Verify its counit equation first on an ordinary module $G$. In the local inverse-image presheaf, a generator at $W\to U$ is represented by $T\to V$, an arrow $W\to u_f(T)$ over $U$, and a section $m\in G(u_f(T))$. Via the canonical pullback square [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism], it is the same generator in the global inverse image with the map to $V$ forgotten. The local counit and the restriction of the global counit both send it to the restriction of $m$ along $W\to u_f(T)$. Hence their maps agree after sheafification; the coefficient actions agree by Step 1. The presheaf formula is [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and the linear adjuncts are [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Apply this equality degreewise to the K-injective $I$ of Step 3. The termwise adjunction and its counit descend to homotopy classes by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Since exact pullback preserves quasi-isomorphisms and $I,j_U^*I$ are K-injective, the Hom bijections of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identify these with the canonical derived adjunctions. Writing $\theta:Lf_V^*j_V^*\cong j_U^*Lf^*$ and $\varepsilon,\varepsilon_V$ for the derived counits, we therefore have
$$\varepsilon_{V,j_U^*E}\,Lf_V^*(\beta_E)=j_U^*(\varepsilon_E)\,\theta_{Rf_*E}.$$
By the bijection defining the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], this identifies $\beta$ with that mate, rather than just some isomorphism between its source and target.

source.place: 04J0 and 03CF with the counit evaluation; 07A6, lemma-adjoint, computed on K-injective representatives

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] for the ringed square of Step 1, with $g=j_V$, $g'=j_U$, $f'=f_V$ and $Q=P$. Steps 2 and 4 supply its canonical derived pullback and tensor comparisons, and Step 5 identifies its exchange with $\beta$. Its equality of the two composites says precisely that the restriction of $\pi_{f,E,P}$, under the comparisons of Steps 2--4, is $\pi_{f_V,j_U^*E,j_V^*P}$. No projection-formula isomorphism is assumed. All comparisons commute with integer shifts: the exact restriction and pullback squares are termwise and send the shifted differential $-d$ to $-j^*d$; the pushforward square on $I[n]$ is the same degreewise identity; and the tensor comparison preserves the bidegrees, hence the usual shift sign $(-1)^{na}$ on the second tensor variable. [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] gives the canonical tensor and projection-mate shift structures for $f$ and $f_V$. The preceding termwise checks identify these structures with their restricted ones, so the equality includes the shift comparisons.

Finally let $a:A\to B$ satisfy the stated local isomorphism condition. Represent it as $Q(h)Q(s)^{-1}$ with $s:C\to A$ a quasi-isomorphism and $h:C\to B$ a cochain map, using the right calculus of fractions [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system, lem-pc-right-fraction-representation]. By exactness of restriction from Step 2, for each $q$ the map $H^q(a)$ restricts to an isomorphism on every member of the specified covering of every $V$. Its inverse section maps are natural on the slices, hence agree after further restriction to $V_i\times_VV_j$ (both are inverses to the same map). The sheaf equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] glues these inverses, giving an inverse to $H^q(a)$ on $V$. Thus $H^q(a)$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves for all $q$. Since $H^q(s)$ is already invertible, $H^q(h)$ is invertible; $h$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Both $Q(h)$ and $Q(s)$ are invertible, so $a$ is invertible. This checks every degree separately; no uniform bound, quasi-compactness, or enough-points assumption has been used.

split_report.summary: Split all three derived comparisons on ordinary localization, exact restriction, K-injective and K-flat representatives. Identified the direct-image comparison as the exchange mate by checking its counit on local section generators; applied the existing generic tensor/exchange coherence and checked shift signs. Proved local detection with sheaf gluing and fractions. One new statement-only node for 04J0; no new elementary or derived-clause restatements.
